source_evidence: Source prescribes MONO-phase TWO conductor circuits, whereas B uses MONO-phase THREE conductor circuits; polyphase <=16Cu/25Al part matches. Could mean PE included as third wire but not the wording of the rule.
A repeats the precise I7 2023 condition: mono-phase TWO conductors regardless of size. B wrongly says mono-phase THREE and uses polyphase 25Cu/35Al vs correct <=16Cu/25Al.
Continuous current carrying ability directly depends on conductor cross-section; circuit length affects voltage drop instead of intrinsic thermal ampacity.
Conductive material Cu/Al changes resistive heating and permissible current, as tabulated in I7 annexes.
Insulation PVC vs XLPE determines temperature limits and permissible current in I7 tables.
Installation/reference laying method controls heat dissipation and admissible continuous current.
For single-phase motor overload protection at least on live conductor not connected to earth; in usual 230V L/N circuits this is phase, not neutral.
Bell transformer or 220V bell may be supplied from normal lighting, socket circuit or direct distribution board. A lists all permitted options.
Bell transformer may be supplied from normal lighting circuit: B is permitted option, whereas alternatives A/C say ONLY another path and are false. B is not exhaustive but not exclusive.
I7 Annex 5.32 visual table shows 2.5 mm2 Cu minimum for single-phase socket phase conductors, no aluminum value specified for this row.
